title: Room Rental and Co-Living Agreement with House Rules
summary: Rent a private room in a shared home, with shared-space rules, utilities, chores, guests and move-out terms.
useWhen: An owner or master tenant rents a bedroom in a home they share, or runs a co-living house where residents share common areas.
watchOuts: Security deposit limits, separate-account and interest rules, and return deadlines vary by state and sometimes by city. Check the state notes before setting the deposit.
Many cities have rent control, just-cause eviction, registration or inspection rules that override lease terms. Verify locally.

Notices of default, eviction or the right to cure for a primary residence are excluded from the federal E-SIGN Act. Serve those notices the way your state's law requires, usually on paper, even if the lease itself is signed electronically.

Fair housing: do not screen, advertise or set terms based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation and gender identity), national origin, familial status or disability, or other classes protected by state and local law. Many places also prohibit discrimination based on source of income.
If you are a tenant renting out a room, your own lease probably requires the landlord's written consent to sublet. Subletting without it can get you evicted.

Some states treat a single roomer in an owner-occupied home as a 'lodger' with faster removal procedures (for example California Civil Code §1946.5). Others give roommates full tenant rights. Verify locally.

The federal Fair Housing Act exempts some owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units from certain rules, but never from its advertising rules. Courts have held that choosing a roommate to share a living unit is outside the Act. State and local laws may still apply.
Stays under 30 days may count as short-term rentals subject to city permits, taxes and bans.
Co-living operators who rent many rooms may be running a rooming or boarding house that needs a license or inspection.

sections.title: 1. Parties and home
sections.body:
**Host:** {{host_name}} ({{host_email}}), who is {{host_status}}.

**Resident:** {{resident_name}} ({{resident_email}})

Host rents to Resident {{room}} (the "Room") in the home at {{home_address}}, in {{state}} (the "Home"), for Resident's personal residence only.

sections.title: 2. Host is a tenant
sections.body: Host rents the Home from a landlord under a separate lease (the "Master Lease"). Host has the landlord's written consent to rent the Room. This agreement is subject to the Master Lease. Resident will follow the Master Lease's rules that Host provides in writing. If the Master Lease ends, this agreement ends too, and Host will give Resident as much notice as possible and refund prepaid rent and the deposit as required by law. Resident: [[initial:resident]]
sections.showIf: host_status == 'a tenant with written landlord consent to sublet'

sections.title: 3. Shared and private space
sections.body: Resident has private use of the Room. Resident may use these shared areas in common with other residents: {{shared_areas}}. Off-limits: {{off_limits}}.

sections.title: 4. Private bathroom
sections.body: Resident also has private use of the bathroom attached to the Room.

sections.title: 5. Furnishings
sections.body: The Room is furnished. Furniture is listed in a move-in inventory signed by both.

sections.title: 6. Term
sections.body: Starts {{start_date}}. Term: {{term_type}}.

sections.title: 7. Fixed term
sections.body: This agreement ends on {{end_date}} unless the parties agree in writing to extend it. After that, it continues month to month.

sections.title: 8. Rent and deposit
sections.body: Rent is {{rent}} per month, due on day {{due_day}}. Late fee after 5 days: {{late_fee}}, where allowed by law. Security deposit: {{deposit}}, returned after move-out minus lawful deductions, with an itemized statement, within the deadline set by the law of {{state}}.

sections.title: 9. Utilities
sections.body: Utilities (electricity, gas, water, trash and internet) are {{utilities}}.

sections.title: 10. Utility cap
sections.body: Rent includes utilities up to {{utility_cap}} per month for the Room's share. If a month's bills exceed the cap, Host may charge Resident its fair share of the excess with copies of the bills.

sections.title: 11. House rules
12. Pet
sections.body: Resident may keep: {{pet_terms}}. Resident is responsible for cleanup, noise and damage.

sections.title: 13. Privacy and entry
sections.body: Host will not enter the Room without at least {{entry_notice_hours}} hours' notice and a reasonable purpose (repairs, inspection or showing), except in an emergency or with Resident's consent. Shared areas may be used by all residents at any time.

sections.title: 14. Repairs and damage
sections.body: Host keeps the Home safe and habitable and makes needed repairs after notice, as the law requires. Resident reports problems promptly and pays for damage Resident or Resident's guests cause beyond normal wear. Resident will not change locks, paint or make alterations without written consent.

sections.title: 15. Housemate disputes
sections.body: Residents will try to resolve disagreements directly and respectfully, then with Host's help. Repeated or serious violations of the house rules are a breach of this agreement after written notice and a chance to correct them.

sections.title: 16. Ending the agreement
sections.body: Either party may end a month-to-month arrangement with at least {{notice_days}} days' written notice, or longer if the law requires. Host may end the agreement for a serious breach only by following the notice and court procedures that apply under the law of {{state}} to the type of occupancy, such as tenant or lodger. Host will never use lockouts, utility shut-offs or removal of belongings to force a move. At move-out, Resident returns all keys and removes all belongings.

sections.title: 17. Required notices
sections.body: Legal notices, such as notices to pay rent or quit, will be delivered as required by the law of {{state}}, which may require paper delivery. Routine messages may be sent by email or text.

sections.title: 18. Lead warning (older homes)
sections.body: If the Home was built before 1978, Host will provide the federal lead-based paint disclosure and EPA pamphlet before Resident signs. Housing built before 1978 may contain lead-based paint. Lead from paint, paint chips, and dust can pose health hazards if not managed properly. Lead exposure is especially harmful to young children and pregnant women. Before renting pre-1978 housing, lessors must disclose the presence of known lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards in the dwelling. Lessees must also receive a federally approved pamphlet on lead poisoning prevention. Resident: [[initial:resident]]

sections.title: 19. State-specific requirements
sections.body: The property is in {{state}}. The parties will comply with that state's requirements for this transaction, including required seller disclosures and forms, licensing rules, closing and recording requirements, and any mandatory statutory notices. Massless shows a summary of known requirements for {{state}} with this template. That summary is a starting point, may be incomplete or out of date, and is not part of this agreement. Any addendum or disclosure form the state requires will be attached and signed by the parties.

sections.title: 20. General
sections.body: This agreement is governed by the law of {{state}} and applicable local law. Terms that conflict with mandatory protections are unenforceable to that extent. It is the entire agreement and may be changed only in writing. Electronic signatures are valid.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

Printed name: [[name:host]]
Date: [[date:host]]

**Resident** — {{resident_name}}

[[sig:resident]]

Printed name: [[name:resident]]
Date: [[date:resident]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything.
